thread:
maria: quick ask — I need to flip on a short-lived capture on prod-proxy to debug a streaming hallucination. plan is: 1) capture streaming response chunks for ~1 hour, 2) include related request headers (X-Request-ID, x-client-id), 3) store minimal user metadata (hashed user_id) and sampling flags. Can security quick-check?

owen: how short-lived is short-lived? who needs access and where will the data land?

maria: planning 1 hour capture, then auto-delete after 7 days. data -> internal s3 debug-bucket (ephemeral prefix). access: engineers on the bug (owen, kevin), and oncall.

kevin: do NOT store Authorization or any Bearer tokens. strip them at proxy before persisting. also do NOT persist full prompt text unless we mask PII. prefer storing prompt fingerprints or truncated prefix <= 128 chars.

jess: +1 on token strip. for prompts: can we pseudonymize by hashing with project-specific HMAC key? helps debugging while avoiding raw user content. retention should be <=24h for streaming chunks ideally.

sec-bot: security checklist: remove/obfuscate Authorization and cookie headers; hash user identifiers with HMAC(KMS); redact emails and phone numbers in prompt/response samples (regex + email/phone heuristics); do not capture embeddings or raw tokens that contain long user text without consent. ensure s3 bucket has limited IAM role and temporary STS creds only.

maria: thanks. plan update: proxy will strip Authorization, cookie, and x-session before write. user_id -> HMAC-SHA256 with customer-debug-key (KMS). prompts: store first 120 chars + hashed remainder. responses: store streaming chunks but with PII scrub regex. retention 7 days on bucket, but we'll enforce a cron to delete after 24h for this capture. access via ephemeral pre-signed URLs only.

sanjay: I can approve this with the following conditions: 1) KMS policy must prevent key export, 2) provide a short doc with exact scrub regex and example samples, 3) ops must provision temporary access and revoke immediately after debugging window. ping me when the doc is up.

mike: where will logs/metadata go? also we need to ensure tracing headers (X-Request-ID) are preserved so we can correlate without storing user content.

maria: storing X-Request-ID, model, route, and hashed user_id. no raw prompt beyond 120-char prefix.

kevin: add a checksum (not reversible) of the full prompt (SHA256) so we can detect duplicates without seeing text. good for regression grouping.

jess: please add example of a redacted sample in the doc (before/after). also note: if any EU traffic may trigger extra compliance review — flag if you expect EU users in the sample.

maria: noted — most repros are US-only but will confirm. I'll post the scrub regex + sample file in this thread within 20m. tagging @sanjay for final sign-off once posted.

sec-bot: reminder: create a ticket in SEC-OPS with the s3 prefix and IAM role before capture starts. automated check will block if KMS/HSM rules not met.

maria: created SEC-OPS-8472 and added details. doc: https://internal.redwood/sec/SEC-OPS-8472 (link)

sanjay: reviewed the doc quick-pass, looks good. approve for 1h capture window. please run the cron to purge after 24h and paste the purge job command here when running.

maria: will run purge job: `aws s3 rm s3://debug-bucket/prod-proxy/2061234567 --recursive --profile ephemeral-debug && echo purged` and will paste logs when done. starting capture at 15:10 PST. thanks all :thumbsup:

owen: thanks — ping if you need help verifying scrubbed samples.

kevin: one last nit — add a flag to avoid sampling any user-supplied files or attachments.

maria: done, adding to doc. ending thread after capture complete.
